subject: Aureus model-fit recap & parity decision plan
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@aureusfin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: model-fit assessment + next steps

Hi Samira / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and a suggested, short evaluation path so you can get a decision signal without a long pilot. TL;DR: we see two open candidates that look promising vs your internal baseline; we recommend a focused parity gate (5k prompts) plus a small canary in production if metrics hold.

What we covered
- Main AU requirements: invoice understanding, multi-turn billing Q&A, and rare-edge regulatory wording (AML flags).
- Your current internal baseline: AureusX-v1 (proprietary), strong on recall but expensive to run.
- OPS constraints: target 95th pctl latency < 250ms for short queries, per-request inference cost target <$0.03.

Open model candidates we suggest testing first
- Llama-3-13B-q4 (quantized): good token economy, strong instruction-following in our prompt bundles.
- Mistral-Instruct-7B (int8): compact, lower cost for short queries; may underperform on rare-edge long context.

Acceptance scorecard (proposed parity thresholds)
- Accuracy (intent classification + answer correctness): >= 92% relative to AureusX-v1 on held prompt set
- Hallucination rate (factual errors on labeled set): <= 2.0% absolute
- Latency: median < 200ms, 95th < 300ms on your expected QPS profile
- Token cost: per-response cost delta <= 0.40x of AureusX-v1 (i.e., cheaper is fine, small regressions allowed if cost savings > 30%)

Concerns to validate during the gate
- Quality regressions on regulatory phrasing — we’ll instrument a focused suite of 300 labeled prompts that exercise AML/terms language.
- Multi-turn statefulness — KV cache behavior when customers bounce between invoice threads.
- Rare-edge hallucination patterns on entity normalization (IBANs, tax IDs).

Proposed next steps (owners & timeline)
1) Redwood runs 5k prompt parity test on both open candidates using the attached prompt bundle (owner: Ben) — results in 3 business days.
2) If scorecard passes, run a 48-hour canary against 10% traffic in your staging environment (owner: Marissa) — 1 week.
3) Pricing/operational estimate and slot sizing (owner: Laura) — share cost_estimate_playbook.xlsx by EOD Friday.

Attachments: aureus_prompt_bundle_v1.csv (prompt sets + labels), benchmark_summary_v1.pdf (baseline test plan)

If this plan looks reasonable I’ll kick off the 5k runs first thing tomorrow and share the initial spreadsheet with per-prompt deltas.

Thanks —
Laura
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference

Really helpful, thanks. A couple quick asks before you run:
- Can you include per-prompt hallucination tags in the output CSV so we can do a secondary audit?
- For the cost comparison, please show end-to-end estimated cost (including network egress and tokenization overhead) not just per-token model cost.
- Any idea on how the open candidates handle redaction of PII in conversational replies? We need a short summary.

If those are covered, green to go on the 5k run.

Samira

Laura / Ben —

On the operational side I recommend we run the 5k parity jobs in parallel across both candidates and produce one consolidated sheet with the following columns: prompt_id, prompt_text (hash), aureusx_answer, candidate_answer, correctness_flag (0/1), hallucination_flag (0/1), latency_ms, token_cost_usd. Ben — can you also include a small column with the prompt family tag (invoice, regulatory, general) so Samira can filter quickly.

For canary sizing: 10% of staging QPS for 48h should be enough to see tail latency and transients. If the open candidate misses the hallucination gate by a small margin but saves >40% cost, we should consider an augmented hybrid approach (AureusX fallback for flagged prompts).

I’ll add a pricing sketch to cost_estimate_playbook.xlsx and flag where reserved capacity vs burst would change unit economics.

Marissa
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
